title: Lighting, Sightlines and Access: Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design for East Bay Rentals

findings.quote: No law requires a CPTED review
findings.root_cause: The conclusion turns a narrowly framed voluntary maintenance checklist into an unsupported universal legal exemption (STD-HONEST). Oakland expressly requires CPTED assessment for a particular vehicle-barrier obstruction-permit process. That does not establish a routine inspection duty for every rental, but defeats the blanket wording. Source: https://www.oaklandca.gov/Public-Safety-Streets/Transportation-Permits-Engineering/Obstruction-Permit
findings.fix: Replace with: "Use this checklist as a voluntary maintenance self-audit. If you plan alterations or permit work, ask the city whether project-specific CPTED review or other conditions apply." In FAQ 5 replace the first sentence with: "Oakland's CPTED checklists are written for development projects; here, we use the residential checklist as a voluntary maintenance self-audit for an existing rental."
findings.future_prevention: Keep maintenance recommendations separate from claims that no law or permit condition applies.

findings.quote: Entries, walkways, mail areas and parking should be lit from dusk to dawn.
findings.root_cause: The standalone spoken script omits the best-practice label that distinguishes recommendations from law in the article. EVD-CONFIDENCE-LEVELS applies to the script as well as the body.
findings.fix: Replace the script sentence with: "As a best practice, we recommend steady dusk-to-dawn lighting at entries, walkways, mail areas and parking." On the video page, replace the corresponding takeaway with: "Best practice: provide steady dusk-to-dawn lighting at entries, walkways, mail areas and parking."
findings.future_prevention: Check confidence labels in both copies of the script and in standalone takeaways.

findings.quote: Trim shrubs near paths and windows to about 2 feet, and tree canopies to about 6 feet
findings.root_cause: The owner checklist drops the word clearance, making the six-foot figure read as tree height rather than the open space beneath the canopy. Other passages and the script state the distinction better. STD-PRACTICAL / GATE-LOCAL-ACCURACY. Source: https://www.oaklandca.gov/files/assets/city/v/1/planning-amp-building/documents/sp/design-standards/cpted-residential.pdf
findings.fix: Replace with: "Keep shrubs near paths and windows about 2 feet high, and maintain about 6 feet of clear space beneath tree canopies, following Oakland's CPTED guideline."
findings.future_prevention: Preserve the measured dimension when shortening guidance; use the same correction in the package's Instagram checklist.

claim_provenance.quote: Our tenants see the property after dark every night; we mostly see it in daylight. So we rely on them to tell us what's wrong. Our October tenant newsletter asks residents to submit a maintenance request whenever an exterior light is out, flickering or on a timer that's no longer set right, and to report any front door, gate or lobby door that isn't latching on its own. The line we use with tenants: we can only fix what we know about.
claim_provenance.source: knowledge/company/anecdote-log.md — 2026-10-16 entry; same-day broken-lock policy additionally documented 2026-09-30
claim_provenance.note: Internal documented record, not AI-assigned owner verification. The tenant-reporting line is company practice, not a claim of routine night inspections.

claim_provenance.quote: Two things follow from that. First, a tenant report is notice. Once someone tells us an entry light is out or a lobby door won't latch, we know about it, and the clock is running. That's why we treat a broken entry or lobby lock as an emergency, with a vendor sent the same day. Company policy. Second, making it easy for tenants to report is part of the security plan, not just customer service. If tenants don't know how to report a dark walkway, or don't think anyone will act on it, the problem stays invisible to the owner.
